h1: Can You Use Olive Oil in an Air Fryer?
excerpt: An air fryer needs a teaspoon of oil on the food, not a pour in the basket, and how you put it on matters more than which grade you reach for.
keyTakeaway: Olive oil belongs in an air fryer on the food, never in the basket. Brush or toss roughly a teaspoon over a full basket, keep aerosol cans away from the coating, and set the dial at 180 to 200°C for most things. Coat anything dry and starchy; leave wet batter to a pan.
heroAlt: A green kitchen basket holding cooked potato wedges on a wooden counter, a small spoon and a single olive beside it, an oven in the background.
inlineAlt: Close view of potato wedges on a metal air fryer tray being brushed with olive oil using a silicone pastry brush.
intro: The air fryer has become a fixture on Malaysian kitchen counters, and nobody was given instructions for it. It is a small fan oven, not a fryer, and its oil does a different job from the oil in a wok.
Yes, olive oil works in one. What changes is the quantity and how it goes on.

sections.heading: How much olive oil an air fryer basket takes

blocks.text: A full air fryer basket needs roughly one teaspoon of olive oil, tossed through the food before it goes in. The machine moves hot air rather than submerging anything, so oil not clinging to a surface drains to the drawer and burns there. Toss until each piece is glossy.

items: **One teaspoon** for a basket of chips, wedges or florets.
**Half a teaspoon** for chicken, which releases its own fat.
**A brushed film** for bread, halloumi or anything already coated.
**None** for reheating something fried once already.

sections.heading: Why aerosol sprays wreck an air fryer basket

blocks.text: Commercial cooking sprays carry more than oil. Propellants and additives such as lecithin land as a fine mist on the basket coating, bake on and build a sticky brown film that washing will not shift. Manufacturer manuals commonly warn against them. Use a pump mister or a silicone brush.

sections.heading: What an air fryer runs at, against what the oil takes

blocks.text: An air fryer dial climbs higher than an olive oil coating ever needs. Set 180 to 200°C for chips, wedges, root vegetables and chicken, and 160 to 170°C for fish, bread and anything that browns quickly. Leave the top of the dial for cooking with nothing brushed on.

While the food is still giving off steam, the oiled surface stays below the air temperature. The bare patches of a half-loaded basket scorch first. For figures by grade, read [olive oil smoke point](/blog/olive-oil-smoke-point-what-heat-it-can-take).

sections.heading: Which foods take olive oil well in an air fryer

blocks.text: Dry, starchy and firm foods take olive oil best, because there is a surface for it to hold and something for the heat to crisp. Potatoes, root vegetables, cauliflower, chickpeas, chicken thighs, prawns and thick bread all work. Wet batter does not, and loose flour blows onto the element.

items: Cut and dry the food, since a damp surface steams before it browns.
Toss it with the oil and salt in a bowl, off the machine.
Load one layer only, with gaps for the air to move.
Shake the basket once halfway, then drizzle raw oil over it afterwards.

sections.heading: Which grade goes in the basket

blocks.text: Extra virgin is the grade to reach for, because the quantity is so small. A teaspoon over a full basket is not where a bottle disappears, and the coating is doing a mechanical job: drying the surface, helping it brown, keeping it off the metal.

What the fan does take is the aroma, which fades at 200°C whichever grade goes in. So hold a spoonful back and drizzle it over the food once the basket is out. Sizes and prices are on the [Arabian Village product page](/products).

sections.heading: Keeping the drawer clean when you cook with oil

blocks.text: Oil that misses the food collects in the drawer under the basket, and left there it bakes into a varnish that smokes on the next run. Wash the basket and drawer after any oiled cook, while both are still warm. Soapy water and a soft brush is the job.

items: Wipe the drawer out first, so grease does not go down the sink.
Never use steel wool or a scouring pad on the coating.
Dry both parts before they go back in a humid kitchen.

blocks.text: A teaspoon on the food, never a pour in the basket. A brush or a bowl, not an aerosol can. Extra virgin for that teaspoon, a spoonful more once it is out, and a wash while it is warm. See also [cooking with olive oil in a Malaysian kitchen](/blog/how-to-cook-with-olive-oil-in-a-malaysian-kitchen).

faqs.q: Can you put olive oil in an air fryer?
faqs.a: Yes, on the food rather than in the basket. Toss or brush about a teaspoon over a full basket before cooking. Oil poured straight into the basket drains into the drawer below and burns there instead of crisping anything at all.

faqs.q: Can I use extra virgin olive oil in an air fryer?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is the grade to use. A teaspoon over a full basket is a small amount, and at the usual 180 to 200°C it copes with the heat. The aroma fades under the fan, so keep a spoonful back for afterwards.

faqs.q: Why should I not use olive oil spray in an air fryer?
faqs.a: Aerosol cans carry propellants and additives alongside the oil. Those settle on the basket coating, bake on and build a sticky film that will not wash off, so the surface stops releasing food properly. A refillable pump mister avoids it.

faqs.q: How much oil does an air fryer basket need?
faqs.a: About one teaspoon for a full basket of chips or vegetables, and roughly half that for chicken, which releases its own fat as it cooks. If oil is still pooling in the mixing bowl after tossing, the amount was too high.

faqs.q: What temperature should I set for olive oil in an air fryer?
faqs.a: Use 180 to 200°C for potatoes, chicken and root vegetables, and 160 to 170°C for delicate items such as fish or bread. Leave the very top of the dial for cooking with nothing brushed on, where there is no oil on the surface to scorch.

faqs.q: Should I preheat the air fryer before adding oiled food?
faqs.a: A three-minute preheat helps things crisp rather than dry out, and costs very little. Oil the food while the machine warms, then load it in one layer. Never leave an oiled basket heating on its own with nothing in it.
